subject.title: Android: gateway pairing UX trails iOS (duplicate buttons, no discovered list, buried setup code)

question: Should the Android pairing-parity work live primarily in the existing Connect tab, in Gateway Settings as proposed, or as a deliberately shared surface with one canonical implementation?
rationale: Current documentation says gateway controls were moved to Connect to de-duplicate Settings, while the linked PR restores a substantial pairing workflow inside Gateway Settings; code review alone cannot choose that permanent product boundary.

options.title: Keep Connect canonical
options.body: Retarget the parity UX to Connect and leave Settings as status or navigation so pairing logic and actions have one owner.

options.title: Adopt Gateway Settings
options.body: Accept Gateway Settings as the primary pairing surface and update or simplify Connect plus documentation to avoid duplicate flows.

options.title: Share a common component
options.body: Expose entry points in both locations but render one shared pairing component and state model with explicit navigation and tests.

recommendation.title: Keep Connect canonical
recommendation.body: Retarget the parity UX to Connect and leave Settings as status or navigation so pairing logic and actions have one owner.

likelyOwner.reason: The Android README identifies @obviyus as the app maintainer, and the decision spans the Android Connect and Settings information architecture.
